The petitioners in Mvc No.5947/202 & Mvc
No.5948/2022 have filed these petitions under
Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming
compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- and Rs.8,00,000/-
respectively for the injuries sustained by them in a
road traffic accident.
2 .  These two petitions are arising out of the same accident.
Hence, these petitions are clubbed and taken together for common discussion for the sake of convenience and to avoid the repetition.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
 3.

That on 10.10.2022 at about 00.10 a.m. the petitioners in both the cases were proceeding in a car bearing No.KA-40-M-8663 from Bengaluru- Chikkaballapur, NH-44 road, when they reached  3 SCCH-18 MVC 5947/2022 & 5948/2022 near Avathi Village bridge, at that time, driver of the Private Bus bearing registration No.NL-07-B-0821 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car.
Due to the said impact, the petitioners were sustained grievous injuries.

This accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Private Bus bearing registration No.NL-07-B-0821.
 4.

20 . On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioners.
But strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

21. On rival contentions of both the parties, in order to find out the truth, for the final determination of the above point, it is necessary to appreciate the evidence given by both the parties in order to come to the proper conclusion.

22. The petitioners herein, to discharge the burden lies on them, relied on the affidavit evidence and have examined as PW1 & PW2 wherein, they reiterated the main petition averments with regard  9 SCCH-18 MVC 5947/2022 & 5948/2022 to the accident.

Hence, I am of the view that the petitioners have proved that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the driver of the Private Bus bearing registration No.NL-07-B-0821.

Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him, in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
11 SCCH-18 MVC 5947/2022 & 5948/2022  Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held  that, the court has to make judicious attempt  to award compensation to the loss suffered  by the claimant.
The compensation should  not be assessed conservatively.
On the other  hand, compensation should also not be  endeavouring to secure some uniformity and  consistency.
The object of awarding  compensation is to make good the loss  suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as  money can do so, in a fair reasonable and  equitable manner."

"while determining  quantum of compensation, in such cases, the  court has to strike a balance between the  inflated and unreasonable demands of a  victim and the equally untenable claim of the  opposite party saying that nothing is  payable.
That sympathy for the victim does  not, and should not, comes in the way of  making a correct assessment.
But if a case is  made out, and the court must not be chary of  awarding adequate compensation.

LIABILITY:
 51.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Private Bus bearing registration No.NL-07-B-0821 the alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

52. The respondent No.2 has contended that,
this respondent has not issued any policy of  22 SCCH-18 MVC 5947/2022 & 5948/2022 insurance in respect of bus bearing No.NL-07-B- 0821.
In this regard, it has examined Assistant Manager as RW1.

He has stated that respondent No.2 has not issued any policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.NL-07-B-0821 infavour of the respondent No.2 and the policy No.9897868899697969/GHR mentioned in the claim petition is not correct and not pertaining to the bus bearing No.NL-07-B-0821.

He has placed authorisation letter, notice u/s 133 of MV Act and reply notice u/s 133 of MV Act, letter,
verification document, premium payment statement and verification document which are marked at Ex.R1 to Ex.R7.
At the time of cross-examination RW1 admitted that in Ex.R3 policy number and the name of the company mentioned.
Further denied the suggestion that at the time of taking B extract from Bengaluru-one, the name of the company and the policy number will be seen.
Further denied that Ex.R7 print out can be taken form your company as per your convenience.
53. The learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners have proved their case by placing cogent and corroborative evidence and are entitled for compensation.
The insurance policy belongs to respondent No.2 and is liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioners.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the insurance company ha  23 SCCH-18 MVC 5947/2022 & 5948/2022 Krishnappa.A vs M. Salahuddin on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19674842/
15 snot issued any policy in respect of offending vehicle.

Therefore, respondent no.2 is not liable to pay compensation on behalf of respondent No.1.
 54.
On perusal of the documents placed by the RW1, it is clear that as on the date of accident there is no insurance policy to the vehicle bearing No.NL- 07-B-0821.
The said fact has not disputed by the respondent No.1, who being the owner of the offending vehicle.
If the policy number and the validity of the policy as mentioned in Ex.R3 is correct, he would have appeared before this court and challenged the Ex.R3 and its contents.
For the reasons best known to him, he has not turned up and remained absent, placed exparte.

Hence,
respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.

55. In the light of the discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, shall satisfy the compensation amount awarded to the petitioner along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its realization.
On the other hand, in view of absence of insurance policy, as on the date of the accident, the insurance company, the respondent No.2 is absolved of its liability.
And there is no exceptional circumstance forthcoming in the case on hand, to follow the principle of pay and  24 SCCH-18 MVC 5947/2022 & 5948/2022 recovery.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No. 3 in both the cases;
 56.

In view of the above discussions on issue No.1 & 2 in both the cases, I proceed to pass the following;
